definitions.openingPairs: core.pairs(initialBoard).length; excludes no pair known to actual enumerator
definitions.openingPairsPerOccupied: Number of legal pairs divided by occupied digit count; a descriptive normalization, not probability or human difficulty.
definitions.openingPairsAmongAllUnorderedDigits: Number of legal pairs divided by n*(n-1)/2; a descriptive edge density.
definitions.witness: The actual generator-returned winning proof, not a shortest route and not proof of minimum required Adds.
definitions.newlyEnabledPairsAfterRemoval: After actual removal and row compression, stable endpoint-ID pair edges absent before the removal. Counts event occurrences, so an edge can count again if lost and re-enabled later.
definitions.newlyEnabledPairsBeforeCompression: Edges newly legal after zeroing the two digits, before compression; these may disappear again during compression.
definitions.newlyEnabledPairsByCompression: Edges after compression absent in the zeroed but uncompressed intermediate state.
definitions.pairIdentity: Persistent ID per logical cell; whole removed rows delete IDs; appended clones receive fresh IDs. Reconstructed row filtering is asserted equal to actual removePair output at every action.
definitions.gapMoves: Exact legacy content.json metric retained for comparison: max(abs(dr),abs(dc)) > 1 OR reading-order index distance > 1. It also counts reading-order adjacent row-boundary pairs with no intervening logical cells.
definitions.throughEmptyCellsMoves: Number of removals with at least one intermediate empty logical cell on the legal path selected by actual checkPair; for reading path, abs(b-a)-1; for straight path, max(abs(dr),abs(dc))-1.
definitions.readingBoundaryAdjacentMoves: Reading-order pairs with abs(b-a) == 1. These explain every extra legacy gapMoves count over throughEmptyCellsMoves in this audit.
definitions.singleLegalRemovalRun: Consecutive witness removals whose actual pre-state has exactly one legal pair; interrupted by Add or a state with more than one legal pair. No claim of human obviousness.
definitions.greedyFailure: This deterministic first-pair policy is blocked after at most two Adds; it is not a proof of board unsolvability.
definitions.fixtureSelection: Extremal controlled examples selected from the sample; not population-effect estimates or independently randomized A/B tests.
definitions.compressionCounts: Include final board clear and removal of a partial final row.
definitions.compressionTopologyChange: At least one surviving endpoint-ID legal pair appears or disappears when empty rows are removed, compared with the same zeroed digits before compression; deleting the selected pair alone does not count.

limits: Node execution of exact source, not a measured phone or production-user result.
Each seed starts with an empty recent-history list; this does not validate long persisted sessions.
A single chosen witness and one fixed greedy policy describe continuation behavior, not universal difficulty.
No human playtest, completion-time estimate, minimum-Adds proof or exhaustive solution-tree census is claimed.
Zero fallbacks in 1000 starts per level does not prove zero fallback probability.
Legacy catalog is audited as reference content; this does not assert it is the current runtime source of starts.
